symptom: On iPhone, room and suite galleries are uncomfortable to swipe, have no visible arrows, and do not present a coherent mobile full-screen viewer and all-images flow.
expected_behavior: Every vacation unit gallery provides a mobile-first full-screen viewer with visible arrows, deliberate one-image swipes, counts, category context, an all-images grid, and context-preserving close and return behavior.
environment: Public-baseline release candidate 559 at commit 27e1fdb456c60dae5e7a5b331becc7af06c44b0c, iPhone-class 390px viewport, vacation business detail pages.

steps: Open a vacation place page on iPhone
Open a room or suite image
Attempt to navigate by finger and look for arrow controls
Switch between the single-image and all-images views
reproduction.evidence: User-supplied iPhone screenshots and direct source inspection of the shared gallery component and mobile CSS.

observations.observation: The shared component renders previous and next buttons without child content.
Mobile CSS explicitly hides the pseudo-element that supplies the desktop arrow glyph.
Swipe detection only compares touch-end X to touch-start X and does not discriminate vertical movement or pointer cancellation.
Two overlapping mobile breakpoint blocks assign conflicting display behavior to the tour and stage.
observations.evidence: app/globals.css max-width 760 and later max-width 560 rules.

hypotheses.mechanism: Mobile CSS converts arrow buttons into invisible edge tap zones by hiding their only glyph and removing the circular control styling.
hypotheses.prediction: Buttons exist and can receive clicks but no visible arrows appear on iPhone.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Inspect rendered controls and computed mobile CSS, then add explicit glyph content independent of pseudo-elements.
hypotheses.result: Supported. Source inspection found empty buttons plus a mobile display:none rule for their pseudo-element. The repaired 390px screenshot shows explicit 48px circular arrows, including the disabled boundary state.

hypotheses.mechanism: The simplistic touch delta handler treats diagonal gestures as navigation and has no vertical-intent guard.
hypotheses.prediction: A sufficiently large X delta can navigate even when vertical movement dominates, producing inconsistent finger behavior.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Exercise horizontal, vertical, diagonal, short, and rapid gestures before and after a pointer-based gesture guard.
hypotheses.result: Supported. The original handler compared X only. The browser audit proves that a vertical-dominant gesture leaves the index unchanged and a horizontal gesture advances exactly one image.

hypotheses.mechanism: Unit-specific state is lost because the shared component is reused without a unit topic.
hypotheses.prediction: Opening different units shows all unit images or stale titles.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Trace both launch paths and component keys, then open two different units sequentially.
hypotheses.result: Rejected. Both launch paths set galleryTopic and key the component by topic; the browser audit opened two different units sequentially and observed fresh titles and indices.

fix.change: Rendered explicit logical arrow glyphs inside 48px controls, separated the mobile grid and viewer states, added a media wrapper so the image begins directly below the tabs, normalized the all-images grid to two columns, and replaced X-only touch handling with guarded pointer gestures.
fix.evidence: Build passed; 12 gallery-family tests passed; scripts/audit-mobile-unit-gallery.mjs passed 11 natural-destination checks and produced inspected 390px viewer and grid screenshots.

regression_checks.evidence: Browser audit opened Terra Suite from vacation-2356 with its unit title, 1/33 count and focused viewer.
Synthetic touch-pointer audit kept the index on vertical movement and advanced exactly one on horizontal movement.
Browser audit switched to the two-column grid, selected thumbnail 2 and returned to 2/33.
Browser audit opened the second room trigger and observed a different unit title.

regression_checks.check: RTL, LTR, low-height and responsive transitions
regression_checks.evidence: Browser audit verified logical arrow sides in both directions, 390x640 containment and 390 to 1280 to 390 transition with scroll lock restored.

regression_checks.check: Main property gallery and desktop family
regression_checks.evidence: Browser audit reopened the main property gallery without a stale unit topic; build and gallery tests passed.

remaining_unknowns: Physical-device iOS Safari was not directly controlled; Chromium mobile emulation plus pointer semantics and visual screenshots are the available local evidence.
authorization_boundary: Local diagnosis and repair only; no public deployment.
